extraction.agency_name: Office of the Clerk of Circuit Court

findings.title: Collection efforts for certain accounts, and related recordkeeping, were not sufficient to ensure compliance with State regulations.
findings.description: The Office did not issue dunning notices or forward certain accounts to CCU as required; as of December 23, 2013, there were 31,169 accounts totaling approximately $7.8 million due prior to January 2009 that were not subject to collection efforts. Additionally, the Office did not pursue collection of receivables for which a judge ordered deferred due dates; BCSO identified 10,390 open accounts totaling $3.2 million with no due date recorded as of April 2013, and records had not been updated by December 5, 2013.

dollar_amounts.context: accounts totaling approximately $7.8 million due prior to January 2009 not subject to collection efforts
open accounts totaling $3.2 million with no due date recorded in the accounts receivable system

findings.recommendation: pursue collections via dunning notices and forward delinquent accounts to CCU; maintain accounts receivable records which properly account for deferred court fees

findings.title: Adequate accountability and control had not been established over civil court fee collections.
findings.description: The Office lacked adequate accountability and control over civil court fee collections totaling $1.2 million during fiscal year 2013, including failing to review employee access capabilities on the automated cash register system where over 800 individuals had access and 7 employees could perform incompatible functions. Additionally, civil court fees received by mail were not restrictively endorsed immediately upon receipt.

dollar_amounts.context: civil court fee collections during fiscal year 2013

findings.recommendation: periodically review employee access capabilities for the automated cash register system and ensure duties are properly separated; take immediate action to address specific access deficiencies; restrictively endorse checks immediately upon receipt

findings.title: The Office’s procedures did not sufficiently ensure the propriety of disbursements to jurors.
findings.description: The Office did not sufficiently ensure the propriety of juror disbursements totaling approximately $835,000 during fiscal year 2013; specifically, supervisors used system-generated attendance reports rather than independent records for verification, and duties were not adequately segregated for Grand Jury disbursements.

dollar_amounts.context: Petit Jury juror disbursements during fiscal year 2013
Grand Jury jurors disbursements during fiscal year 2013

findings.recommendation: use juror attendance records maintained by the check-in clerk to verify propriety of Petit Jury disbursements; separate responsibilities for collecting Grand Jury attendance data and processing information for payment

extraction.agency_response_summary: The report states that the Judiciary's response to findings and recommendations is included in an appendix, but the content of the response is not provided in this text.
